video.title: People Are Selling One Prompt Websites for $1K+ (Full Tutorial)

summary: A sponsored tutorial in which Chris Koerner uses the AI website builder Wegic (transcribed as Ouijic/Weedic) to build a site for his planned Secret Pickleball club, with court booking, leaderboard and members-only merch, in about two and a half minutes, then a Dallas pizza restaurant site with payment buttons, menu and a lead-capture chatbot in about one minute. He pitches it as a way to save $3-5k on a designer or to start a web design agency selling sites for thousands of dollars. His advice is to pick an industry you understand, dig into owners' booking and lead-handling headaches with why/how/who questions, and price on value rather than time. Evidence is promotional: the video is an ad for Wegic.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; demonstrating a sponsor's AI website builder

ideas.name: AI-built website design agency
ideas.one_liner: Use an AI website builder to produce small-business sites in minutes and charge agency prices of thousands per client.
ideas.customer: Small local businesses in an industry you understand (e.g. pizza shops, clubs)
ideas.problem: Owners pay designers $3-5k and wait; they have booking, payment and lead-handling headaches they often can't articulate
ideas.offer: Responsive website with booking, payments, menus, reviews and lead-capture chat, iterated quickly with prompts

price_points.label: typical agency price to match or beat

pricing.notes: Do not undercut just because you build faster; speed can justify charging more.

acquisition_channels.details: Not specified; advice is to talk to owners in a familiar industry and discover problems through questioning.

ideas.delivery: Agency owner prompts Wegic to generate and edit sites, adds payments (Stripe) and forms, publishes.
unit_economics_claims: First website free on Wegic; regenerating a section costs 5 credits

acquisition.how: Discovery conversations with owners are human; in the UK cold email only to limited companies, not sole traders, under PECR.

onboarding.how: Intake questionnaire can be automated; requirements still need conversation.

delivery.how: AI builder generates most of the site; human checks design and integrations.

support.how: Prompt-based edits can be done by agents with approval.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; crowded market and commoditising as owners can use the same tools themselves. UK GDPR applies to contact forms and lead data.

risks: Commoditisation: clients can use AI builders themselves
Hard to sustain thousands per site

ideas.problem: Delivery app commissions; manual pickup/delivery handling by phone

acquisition.how: Selling to restaurant owners is relationship-based; UK PECR limits cold email to limited companies.

onboarding.how: Menu and branding intake can be automated.

tactics.name: Use the tool's own suggested prompts
steps: Before prompting a new AI tool, browse the prompts it suggests
Reuse those phrasings to get better output

quote.text: anytime I use a new AI tool, I want to see what prompts it prompts me to use
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Problem discovery with owners
steps: Pick an industry you understand (worked in or around it)
Ask general questions about their business
Dig in with what, why, how, when, who questions (who takes the lead? where does it go?)
Listen for hidden problems (e.g. staff absence losing leads)
Build several site versions quickly with prompts to solve them

quote.text: Don't make the mistake of assuming that their problems are top of mind because they're usually not
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Value-based pricing for fast delivery
steps: Don't discount because AI makes you faster
Sell speed of delivery as a premium

tactics.name: Add small design touches
steps: Prompt for hover effects and animations
Add lead-capture forms and test them end to end

quote.text: I like to call these the moments between the moments
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't assume business owners know their problems; you must dig.

quote.text: a lot of business owners don't know outright what their problems are
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Asking an AI for fake reviews produces visible fake-review labels; placeholder reviews must be replaced (and fake reviews are illegal under UK consumer law, DMCC Act 2024).

lessons.lesson: Charge for value created, not time spent.

quote.text: Remember, we're charging for the value that we create, not for the amount of time that we spend
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pick the industry you understand best; that's your unfair advantage.

quote.text: The one that you understand is the one that you want to pick because it's the one where you will have an unfair competitive advantage
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Try several industries early rather than committing to one.
If one business has a problem, others in the same industry probably do too.
AI makes iteration cheap: four prompts give four alternative designs.

quote.text: If they don't like the first website you build, four more prompts gets you four new websites
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Ship an MVP to get out into the world before polishing.
